title: Battle of the Hotels reaches its heaviest phase
why: RPG-7 rockets first used in Lebanon; Phoenicia and St Georges hotels changed hands repeatedly, with 40-50 bodies recovered at the Phoenicia.

title: Syria organises a ceasefire and a High Military Committee
why: Damascus-brokered truce and committee early in 1976 mark Syria's first mediation role in the war, before its military entry.

title: Lebanese Front blockade of Tel al-Zaatar camp begins
why: Start of the long blockade that preceded the June assault and the August fall of the camp.

title: Muslim soldiers mutiny; Lebanese Arab Army forms under Lt Khatib
why: About 900 soldiers of the 1st Armoured Brigade mutinied at Zahle; army began splitting along communal lines.

title: Lebanese National Movement retakes Holiday Inn for good
why: PLO fighters dislodged Phalangists on 21 March; the hotel stayed in LNM hands afterwards.

title: Battle of the Hotels ends; Beirut stays divided east-west
why: Fighting since 23 Oct 1975 left about 500 LNM and 250 Lebanese Front dead per one account.

title: Beirut split into east and west sectors along the Green Line
why: Demarcation line separated mainly Muslim west from mainly Christian east, and later also Sunni from Shia areas.

title: First Syrian offensive halts after heavy losses
why: Syrian forces, which entered on 31 May, were stopped at places such as Bhamdoun in the first fortnight.

title: Assad says Syria and Lebanon are 'one people'
why: Public statement during the Syrian intervention, cited by critics as a 'Greater Syria' idea.

title: Syria launches late-July drive on LNM strongholds
why: Library of Congress study places the push in late July, before the October offensive.

title: Second Syrian offensive takes central Lebanon and main towns
why: The October push preceded the Arab League's creation of the Arab Deterrent Force.

title: Riyadh summit agrees a peace force for Lebanon
why: Mini-summit (17-18 October) set up the Arab Deterrent Force and a ceasefire framework.

title: Cairo summit endorses the Riyadh decisions
why: Arab League summit (25-26 October) confirmed the force; Syria supplied most of its troops.

title: Arab Deterrent Force deploys in Beirut at 04:30
why: Force of about 35,000 (27,000-30,000 Syrian) took positions; Saudi, Sudanese, Libyan, Emirati and Yemeni units held sectors.

title: Israel presents itself as protector of border enclaves
why: Three Christian-held pockets next to the frontier became zones of de facto Israeli influence, forerunner of the SLA.

title: Haddad's Marjayoun-based force accepts Israeli protection
why: Major Saad Haddad's unit, after leaving Marjayoun late 1976, placed itself under Israeli protection.

title: Arab Deterrent Force at 30,000 troops, 27,000 Syrian
why: Library of Congress figure for the force at the start of 1977.

title: Lebanese Arab Army disbands after leaders are detained
why: Leaders held in Jan 1977 on a trip to meet Assad; released after 18-24 months on condition they resign.

title: Walid Jumblatt takes over PSP and LNM after his father's death
why: Succession in the Druze leadership shaped the later Mountain War and the Chouf administration.

title: ADF and Lebanese Army clash in East Beirut
why: Syrian-led force and army units exchanged fire in February 1978, months before the Hundred Days' War.

title: Operation Litani ends after a week
why: Israeli operation ran 14-21 March, with about 25,000 troops; tolls given as about 1,100 to 2,000.

title: First UNIFIL troops arrive in south Lebanon
why: UN force mandated on 19 March began arriving; its mandate began the same week.

title: PLO accepts ceasefire after meeting UNIFIL commander
why: Truce ended the fighting that followed Litani; Israel handed positions to the SLA by mid-1978.

title: Haddad's force formalised as 'Free Lebanese Army'
why: Militia later named the South Lebanon Army; Israel supplied pay, arms and access through the Good Fence.

title: Litani operation displaces 100,000-250,000 in the south
why: Estimates vary; many sheltered in Beirut suburbs, changing the capital's demography.

title: Hundred Days' War opens with Syrian shelling of East Beirut
why: About 15,000 Syrian troops around Beirut, shelling at times 100 rounds a minute; 200 dead, 400 wounded in one count.

title: Hundred Days' War ends; Syrians leave East Beirut
why: Saudi and Sudanese ADF units replaced Syrian ones in the Christian sector after UNSC Resolution 436.

title: Fairuz stages the operetta Petra in both halves of Beirut
why: Performances in west and east sectors made the singer a non-partisan symbol; she stayed in Lebanon throughout the war.

title: Syria left as the only ADF contingent
why: Sudan, Saudi Arabia and the UAE announced withdrawals in late 1978; by May 1979 only Syrian troops remained.

title: Sarkis and Assad hold cordial talks in Damascus
why: LoC study lists the meeting among the Sarkis-era contacts with Syria.

title: Siege of Zahle opens as Syrian forces move on Phalangist positions
why: Battle ran to 30 June 1981; Zahle was the last Christian-held town in the Bekaa. (corrected from 1980-12-22: CSMonitor dates the Syrian siege from 1 April 1981; the Wikipedia infobox gives 22 Dec 1980)

title: Israel downs two Syrian helicopters; Syria deploys SAM-6 in Bekaa
why: The Syrian missile deployment opened a crisis between Israel and Syria over the Bekaa. (CSMonitor: helicopters downed 28 April; JTA of 29 April reports one on the 28th and one on the 29th)

title: Siege of Zahle ends; Syrians withdraw, internal security forces enter
why: Arab mediation after about 91 days of siege; Lebanese Forces fighters left; one count: about 400 Lebanese Forces, 700 Syrian/PLO and 200 civilian dead.

title: Israeli air force destroys Syrian SAM batteries in the Bekaa
why: Operation Mole Cricket 19: 29 Syrian aircraft and 17 SAM batteries destroyed by one account; other counts of aircraft are higher.

title: Israel-Syria ceasefire announced; Khalde taken
why: Truce covered Syrian forces; Israeli forces captured Khalde near Beirut airport.

title: Ceasefire extended to the PLO, then collapses on 13 June
why: Fighting resumed around Khalde the next day, opening the approach to Beirut.

title: Israeli forces move to cut the Beirut-Damascus highway
why: Operation to take the road isolated Syrian units and tightened the ring on West Beirut.

title: Israel steps up attacks on West Beirut after a 27-day lull
why: Air, naval and artillery bombardment through 10 August; targeting of PLO leaders attempted.

title: Heaviest bombardment of West Beirut halts after Reagan-Begin call
why: At least 300 died on 10-12 August; Israel's cabinet then removed Sharon's command over air, armour and artillery. PLO accepted Habib plan.

title: French contingent of Multinational Force lands in Beirut
why: First MNF troops to arrive, to oversee the PLO evacuation; US Marines landed 25 August, Italians 26 August.

title: Italian troops deploy in Beirut with the MNF
why: Third contingent of the force supervising the PLO departure.

title: PLO evacuation by sea and land completed
why: About 8,500 fighters sailed to Tunisia and 2,500 left overland; siege toll 4,000-5,000 Lebanese civilians in one estimate.

title: First Multinational Force leaves Beirut
why: Troops re-embarked after the PLO evacuation, two weeks before the president-elect was killed.

title: Israeli army enters West Beirut
why: Move came the day after Bashir Gemayel's death and the day before the Sabra and Shatila killings.

title: Israeli forces leave Beirut; reinforced MNF returns
why: About 1,200 MNF troops came back at the government's request, with US, French and Italian contingents.

title: British squadron of about 100 joins the Multinational Force
why: Armoured reconnaissance unit; it left on 2 January 1984.

title: Kahan Commission publishes report on Sabra and Shatila
why: Israeli inquiry into the 1982 camp killings; its report was published on 8 February 1983.

title: Israel decides to pull back from the Chouf
why: Unilateral move to the Awali line opened a vacuum filled by Druze and Lebanese Forces fighters.

title: PSP and allies launch full offensive in the Chouf
why: Mountain War: fighting with Lebanese Forces and army positions after the Israeli pullout of 3 September.

title: Bhamdoun falls to Druze forces
why: Early gain of the Mountain War; Kabr Chmoun fell on 9 September.

title: Kabr Chmoun falls; Lebanese Forces fall back to Deir el-Qamar
why: Retreat concentrated Christian fighters and civilians in the Deir el-Qamar pocket.

title: Lebanese Army pulls back in the mountains
why: Druze advance filled the gap before the fight for Souk el Gharb.

title: US sends emergency arms shipment to the Lebanese Army
why: Resupply ahead of Souk el Gharb; more tanks and howitzers arrived on 1 October.

title: Mountain War uproots about 20,000 Druze and 163,670 Christians
why: Figures from one account; early September fighting killed an estimated 1,500 in two weeks.

title: Jumblatt announces Civil Administration of the Mountain
why: PSP-run authority that funded services through checkpoint tolls until 1990.

title: Battle of Tripoli opens between PLO factions
why: Arafat loyalists faced Syrian-backed dissidents; about 500 killed and 1,500 wounded by late November; half the city displaced.

title: British MNF contingent leaves Lebanon
why: First of the four contingents to depart in 1984.

title: Haddad dies; South Lebanon Army passes to General Lahad
why: Free Lebanon enclave began to fade; the militia was rebranded SLA and survived until 2000.

title: Lebanese Army splits as Muslim and Druze units defect
why: After the 6 February uprising, units joined Amal and PSP militias in West Beirut.

title: Italian MNF contingent withdraws
why: Second contingent to leave; US Marines left on 26 February.

title: US Marines withdraw from Beirut
why: Embassy guards stayed until 31 July; the departure ended the Reagan-era deployment.

title: French MNF contingent withdraws, ending the force
why: Last contingent to leave, after the 23 October 1983 barracks bombing that killed 58 French and 241 US personnel.

title: Michel Aoun becomes Lebanese Army commander
why: Appointment of the officer who later led a rival government and the 1989-90 wars.

title: Israeli phased withdrawal from Lebanon begins
why: First phase of the pullout that ended in June 1985 with a retained security zone.

title: Amal, PSP and communists defeat Al-Mourabitoun in Beirut
why: A week of fighting broke the Sunni militia, a step before the War of the Camps.

title: Israeli forces reach the south Lebanon 'security zone'
why: Border strip held with the SLA until 2000.

title: Sabra camp largely falls to Amal in War of the Camps
why: Fighting began 19 May around Sabra, Shatila and Burj el-Barajneh; Amal declared a ceasefire on 31 May.

title: Amal and Palestinian National Salvation Front sign ceasefire in Damascus
why: Pause ended the first round; clashes flared again in September.

title: Assad brokers truce while moving Syrian troops in covertly
why: Syrian units entered under the guise of the Palestine Liberation Army, months before open intervention.

title: President Frangieh asks Syria to intervene formally
why: Request preceded the 31 May-1 June entry of regular Syrian troops.

title: Israel begins supplying Maronite forces with arms and advisers
why: Israeli aid to Christian militias began in May 1976, alongside Syria's entry on the same side in practice.

title: Lebanese Front meeting lays ground for the Lebanese Forces
why: Joint command council formed after Tel al-Zaatar convinced leaders a unified militia was needed.

title: Battle of Aishiya: PLO and communist militia attack Maronite village
why: Combined force attacked an isolated village in a mostly Muslim area during the Riyadh settlement weeks.

title: Beirut port resumes operations after nine months' shutdown
why: Clashes halted shipping through 1976; a 1977 assessment found no warehouse or equipment intact.

title: Syrian forces occupy An-Nahar's offices; Tueni leaves for Paris
why: Publication suspended for a while; Syrian forces also closed seven newspapers and a magazine in West Beirut, per one account.

title: East Beirut canton founded with its own treasury and Jounieh port
why: Lebanese Forces-run area held over 60% of industrial capacity and about 800,000 residents; ran taxes, ports and services until 1990.

title: Frangieh leaves the Lebanese Front after the Ehden killings
why: Zgharta-based Marada later allied with Syria, ending a Christian front against Damascus.

title: Tigers militia splits from the Lebanese Forces
why: After months of intra-Christian clashes, culminating in July 1980 when Bashir Gemayel's men took over rival forces.

title: At Tiri incident between UNIFIL and Israeli-backed militia
why: One of several clashes in the UN buffer zone, showing Haddad's enclave resisted the UN force.

title: First Zahle ceasefire after 89 killed
why: Fighting resumed on 4 April, with about 150 dead by the night of 5 April.

title: Second Zahle ceasefire; 265 killed since 1 April
why: Count from press reports of 1981: over 1,000 wounded; shelling in the hills continued on 12 and 22 April.

title: Four Iranian embassy staff seized north of Beirut
why: Taken at a Lebanese Forces checkpoint; cited as a motive for the later abduction campaign against Westerners.

title: Fadi Frem elected Lebanese Forces commander
why: Chosen to succeed Bashir Gemayel in command a day before the president-elect's death.

title: Army 6th Brigade under Col. Aoun re-enters West Beirut
why: Operation of 2-15 October 1982 with other army units and ISF, restoring state presence after Israel left the city.

title: Lebanese Forces and PSP fight at Aley until February 1983
why: Fighting rumbled on until 7 February, when Druze fighters overran the town and drove out the Christian garrison.

title: Geagea made LF commander for the Chouf-Aley sector
why: Role in the Mountain War; he later led the Lebanese Forces from 1986 to 1994.

title: Druze overrun Aley and expel Christian garrison
why: Ended seven weeks of fighting begun on 20 December 1982.

title: AUB president David Dodge freed after a year in captivity
why: He was taken on 19 July 1982; the release closed the first hostage case of the decade-long crisis.

title: Lebanese Air Force flies first combat sorties of the war
why: Three Hunter jets with French navy cover struck Druze and Syrian positions in the Chouf; one was shot down.

title: Jumblatt offers to lift sieges of Souk el Gharb and Deir el-Qamar
why: Both had been cut off since September and relied on weekly Red Cross convoys for food and medicine.

title: Beirut disengagement plan announced, then stalled
why: Plan to demilitarise Beirut approved by Israel, Syria, LF, Amal and PSP, but held up by continued fighting.

title: USS New Jersey fires salvo into the Chouf
why: Naval gunfire in support of the Lebanese Army and Marines at Souk el Gharb.

title: Sporadic fighting returns; informal ceasefire frays
why: Druze artillery shelled East Beirut and the Marine positions; US naval guns replied.

title: Druze forces clear Aley and Kfarmatta; Amal takes Khalde
why: Day-two of the February collapse of government positions south and east of Beirut.

title: Damour and Mechref fall; Mountain War ends
why: PSP/PLA took Damour as Christian civilians fled toward Israeli-held ground; Souk el Gharb was the last government-held Chouf town. (Wikipedia: Mechref and Damour fell the day after 14 Feb 1984; UPI 14 Feb 1984 reports Druze militia reaching the sea)

title: CIA station chief William Buckley kidnapped in West Beirut
why: His case, ending with his death in captivity in 1985, became central to the US hostage crisis.

title: Amal raids a hideout and frees two kidnapped men
why: Two of the foreigners seized in February 1984 were rescued after several months in captivity.

title: Fouad Abou Nader replaces Fadi Frem as LF commander
why: Leadership change within the Lebanese Forces before the 1985 internal revolt.

title: Israeli forces leave Sidon; clashes follow in the area
why: Withdrawal was followed by Palestinian-Christian clashes in East Sidon in March.

title: Geagea, Hobeika and Pakradouni rebel against LF leadership
why: Revolt against commander Abou Nader aimed to free the Lebanese Forces from Gemayel's control.

title: AP bureau chief Terry Anderson kidnapped
why: Longest-held Western hostage, freed on 4 December 1991 after 6 years 9 months.

title: Clashes in East Sidon villages after kidnapping of three Christians
why: Palestinian fighters and local Muslim allies fought local Christians weeks after the Israeli pullout.

title: UNRWA's Alec Collett kidnapped with his driver
why: British UNRWA employee; his death was announced in 1986.

title: AUB dean Thomas Sutherland kidnapped near his home
why: Another US hostage in the mid-1980s group, held until 1991.

title: US bans flights to and from Beirut after TWA 847
why: Reagan's order banned all flights to and from Lebanon after the hijacking that landed at Beirut.

title: Damascus summit on Christian-Druze fighting
why: Gemayel, Karami and Assad met to try to end clashes between Lebanese Forces and PSP militias.

title: LBC begins broadcasting from East Beirut
why: Lebanese Forces station broke Télé Liban's monopoly, transmitting without a licence. (Wikipedia and Arab Media & Society: LBC on air August 1985)
dup_of: LBC launches as first private TV network

title: Tripoli fighting between Tawhid and Syrian-allied party
why: Syrian forces entered the city that autumn and broke the Tawhid militia's military power.

title: Four Soviet diplomats kidnapped in Beirut
why: Part of the 1985 wave of kidnappings of foreigners in West Beirut.

title: Lebanese Forces' internal fighting begins as Geagea attacks Hobeika
why: Forces loyal to Gemayel and Geagea attacked Hobeika's base; it ended on 15 January with his flight to Zahle.

title: Islamic Jihad claims execution of French researcher Michel Seurat
why: Claim followed photos released on 10 February; he is recorded as dying in captivity.

title: Third round of fighting in the War of the Camps begins
why: Lasted three days, coinciding with a rocket attack on Kiryat Shmona.

title: Heavy camp fighting resumes a year after the first round
why: Amal received Soviet-made artillery and T-55 tanks via Syria.

title: Syrian commandos deploy with army task force in West Beirut
why: Force with 800 army and ISF personnel cooled the second round of camp fighting.

title: AUB comptroller Joseph Cicippio kidnapped
why: Held until 1991 in the same hostage wave.

title: Hobeika's men try to take Achrafieh; Geagea holds
why: Attempt eight months after his ouster was repelled by the Lebanese Forces under Geagea.

title: Third and deadliest camp battle begins at Rashidieh
why: Amal and local PLO groups fought around Rashidieh camp in Tyre; about 7,500 civilians fled to Sidon by 7 December.

title: Amal and pro-Syrian Palestinians agree ceasefire; Fatah rejects it
why: Arafat's faction refused but passed some positions to Al-Mourabitoun.

title: Tawhid kills 15 Syrian soldiers; Syrian response scatters it
why: Retaliation after a commander's arrest led to a decisive Syrian-led move in Tripoli.

title: Berri ends camp sieges; Syrian commandos enter West Beirut
why: About 7,000 Syrian commandos arrived after a week of fighting.
dup_of: Syrian troops redeploy in West Beirut

title: CGTL conference calls 'no to war, yes to national consensus'
why: One of two 1987 union conferences (May and September) that led to the November general strike.

title: US journalist Charles Glass seized by previously unknown group
why: Another Westerner taken in 1987; the group was believed to be a Hezbollah alias.

title: Teachers begin indefinite strike over wages
why: Strike sat within the 1987 inflation crisis and preceded the 5-10 November general strike.

title: CGTL and PM Hoss reach deal ending the general strike
why: Committee to strengthen the pound and credits for school fees; mass demonstrations had torn down barricades.

title: UN observer Lt Col William Higgins captured in south Lebanon
why: Marine officer serving with the UN mission; later reported killed in captivity.

title: Three French hostages released
why: Kaufmann, Carton and Fontaine were freed by their captors.

title: Amal offensive on Hezbollah opens the 'War of Brothers'
why: Battle for southern Beirut suburbs; Syrian troops deployed on 27 May. Total toll 500-750 dead.

title: War of the Camps ends: 3,781 dead, 6,787 injured
why: Toll for 1985-88 camp fighting; the article notes real numbers are probably higher.

title: Arab League committee starts work on Lebanon
why: Kuwait-chaired panel with Saudi Arabia, Algeria and Morocco prepared the ground for Taif.

title: Damascus Agreement between Amal and Hezbollah
why: Called for return to the pre-April 1988 status quo and a joint operations room against Israel; fighting persisted in places.

title: Aoun offensive on Lebanese Forces; port basin agreed on 24 Feb
why: About 70 killed in initial clashes; LF ceded Beirut port's fifth basin to Aoun after Patriarchate mediation.

title: Aoun's navy starts blockade of militia ports
why: Patrol boats intercepted a ship bound for the PSP's Jieh port; ports at Jieh and Khalde at issue.

title: Aoun closes Beirut airport
why: Closure lasted six months, until 22 September 1989.

title: Syrian army and PSP shell Beirut, Jounieh and Byblos ports
why: Intermittent shelling of Christian-area harbours as Aoun kept up his blockade.

title: Danish tanker Sun Shield sunk off Jounieh
why: Nine crew died; shipping in the Christian ports was hit by the blockade war.

title: US embassy staff airlifted out of Aoun's enclave
why: Ambassador McCarthy and 29 staff left; six-month toll to then given as 828 killed, 2,455 wounded.

title: Beirut airport reopens after six months
why: Reopened with the Saudi-brokered ceasefire accepted by Aoun.

title: Emile Lahoud appointed Lebanese Army commander
why: Named by the Hrawi side, splitting the army from Aoun.

title: Iqlim al-Tuffah fighting resumes
why: More than 3,500 Amal and Palestinian fighters faced 2,000 Hezbollah; reconciliation came in Nov 1990.

title: Aoun orders media not to call Hrawi 'President'
why: Directive to stop using titles for the Taif government shows the contest over legitimacy.

title: Aoun's forces capture Dbayeh
why: Early gain in the intra-Christian war; about 500 killed over two weeks in one count.

title: Aoun declares ceasefire and signals he could accept Taif with amendments
why: Offer came after weeks of fighting that killed over 1,000 in the months that followed.

title: Hrawi government and Geagea agree army takeover of LF barracks
why: Gen. Elie Hayek was mandated to take over barracks in Mount Lebanon.

title: Naccache freed after French presidential pardon
why: Pardoned by Mitterrand on 27 July 1990; his release was among demands tied to the hostage crisis.

title: Aoun takes refuge in the French embassy
why: Broadcast his surrender at 08:30; estimated 800 killed in the assault, more than 250 prisoners executed per one account.
dup_of: Syrian assault on Baabda ends the civil war

title: Militias begin dismantling the Green Line
why: Withdrawal from Beirut done by 13 November, ahead of the 19 November Taif deadline.

title: Militias complete withdrawal from Beirut
why: Done before the Taif deadline of 19 November.

title: Terry Waite released
why: Held 1,763 days; freed with the closing of the hostage crisis in December 1991.

title: Israel opens its 'Good Fence' to the Christian-held south
why: Crossings at Rmaish and Kfar Kila followed in August; goods, workers and patients crossed until 2000.

title: Arab Security Force deploys between East and West Beirut
why: Force under Maj Gen Muhammad Hassan Ghunaim held a neutral zone before the full ADF arrived in November.

title: Sarkis names Col. Ahmed al-Hajj commander of the Arab Deterrent Force
why: Appointment of an officer loyal to Fouad Chehab, two weeks before the force's Beirut deployment.

title: Losses from first 19 months of war put at L£7.5 billion
why: Library of Congress study: about 250 industries destroyed, one-fifth of industry's fixed capital lost.

title: Syrian troops deploy in the Bekaa and near Tripoli
why: Move followed the 21 July Lebanese-Palestinian compromise on a 15 km PLO-free zone near the border.

title: SLA shells UNIFIL headquarters, wounding eight UN soldiers
why: Early sign that the militia and the UN force were at odds over the border zone. (corrected from 1978-04-19: UNIFIL attack record dates the shelling of Naqoura HQ by de facto forces under Maj. Saad Haddad to 18-19 April 1979; six Irish and two Dutch personnel wounded)

title: Roger Assaf sets up the Hakawati theatre house in West Beirut
why: Wartime theatre of political storytelling; Ziad Rahbani's Bennesbeh Labokra Chou? ran for eight months in 1978.

title: Iraq halts imports of Lebanese goods
why: Egypt also froze preferential terms; war-time relabelling hurt the garment industry's reputation, per the Library of Congress study.

title: Israeli forces close the ring around Beirut
why: Encirclement completed seven days after the 6 June invasion; the siege proper began on 14 June.

title: Israel cuts food, water and electricity to West Beirut
why: Seven-week siege: by end-July about 500 buildings destroyed; shelling accused of being indiscriminate.

title: Sharon and Eitan win Begin's backing for a West Beirut assault
why: Cabinet rejected the plan on 16 July over fear of heavy loss of life.

title: Israel, Lebanon and the PLO accept US-mediated evacuation deal
why: Syria had agreed on 7 August; the PLO departure began on 21 August under multinational supervision.

title: UK agrees to join the Multinational Force
why: British squadron arrived in February 1983, bringing the force to four countries.

title: US Marines return fire for the first time in Beirut
why: Marked a shift from peacekeeping toward combat as Druze and Lebanese Army forces fought near the airport.

title: Piccadilly Theatre closes in mid-1980s
why: The 700-seat Hamra venue, where Fairuz staged nine musicals between 1967 and 1978, shut during the war.

title: Maroun Baghdadi's 'Little Wars' screens at Cannes
why: Part of a war-era wave of Lebanese cinema as feature production fell sharply after 1975.

title: Lebanese Front groups move against rival enclaves in Christian areas
why: Operation cut supply routes while the Tel al-Zaatar assault was under way; camp held about 1,500 PLO fighters.

title: Phalange commander William Hawi killed at Tel al-Zaatar; Bashir Gemayel succeeds
why: Battle death of the Kataeb Regulatory Forces chief raised Bashir Gemayel's standing in the Lebanese Front.

title: PLO and Lebanese Arab Army run a short-lived administration in Tyre
why: Took over barracks, set roadblocks and collected port customs; local support faded within the year.

title: ASALA founded in PLO-controlled West Beirut
why: Armenian militia fought alongside the LNM and PLO, notably against Israeli forces in 1982.

title: Lebanese National Resistance Front formed under Walid Jumblatt
why: Leftist alliance succeeded the LNM and carried out attacks on Israeli forces from 1982 to 1985.

title: Voice of the Mountain radio starts from the Chouf
why: Station of the PSP-run Civil Administration of the Mountain; ran until 1994.

title: Pound at about LL 4.31 to the dollar
why: Library of Congress series: LL 2.3 before the war, 3.81 at end 1982, then a steep fall from 1984.

title: Unemployment at 40% in the 500,000-strong private workforce
why: Industry ran at about 40% of capacity as the middle class was hit for the first time.

title: Pound loses 85% of its remaining value in 1986
why: Library of Congress study: loss of 60% in 1985 and 85% in 1986; per-capita income put at about $250.

title: Pound reaches LL 36.50 per dollar, then 47 within two weeks
why: Step in the fall that took the rate to LL 500 in 1987.

title: Parliament bars sale of BDL gold without a law (Law 42/1986)
why: Passed as the pound collapsed and Governor Naim and Finance Minister Chamoun disagreed on the response.

title: Lebanese Forces take control of Beirut port from mid-1986
why: Held until 1989, when Aoun's army pressed them to withdraw; basin revenue estimated at $300,000 a month in one source.

title: Pound passes LL 250 per dollar
why: Seven months after crossing 100; end-October rate about LL 500.

title: Pound averages about LL 497 per dollar in 1989
why: Rate cited at the turn to the last war year; it passed LL 2,500 in 1992. (corrected from "about LL 900 per dollar", 1989-12: IMF series gives annual averages of 496.69 in 1989, 695.09 in 1990 and 928.23 in 1991; the cited Wikipedia page gives LL 900 for Dec 1989, a figure other sources contradict; read via search excerpt, page not fetchable)

title: Fighting breaks out again in Iqlim al-Tuffah
why: Amal-Hezbollah clashes ran into January 1989 with over 140 killed.

title: Syria and Iran broker Amal-Hezbollah reconciliation
why: Ended the 1988-90 War of Brothers, whose toll is given as 500-750 dead.

title: Grid destroyed by war; cuts reach about 18 hours a day
why: Armed groups took over EDL plants and supplied areas they held; account from HRW's 2023 electricity report.

title: Bodies of three AUB-linked men found after US raid on Libya
why: A group claimed it executed them in retaliation, opening a new round of hostage-taking.
